name: OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance
version_or_profile: OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance 1.0 Final, frozen Registry pre-authorized-code profile
surfaces: credential issuer and authorization server metadata

evidence_docs.label: OID4VCI metadata implementation and contract tests
OID4VCI public route and proof tests

notes: The separate `registry-evidence-oid4vci` supporting service implements a frozen subset of OID4VCI 1.0 Final for holder-bound Evidence credentials. The profile permits issuer-initiated anonymous pre-authorized-code delivery, a stateless nonce, ES256 JWT proofs with an inline public JWK or self-contained `did:jwk#0`, and plural `dc+sd-jwt` credentials. It excludes authorization code, PAR, DPoP, remote DID resolution, other credential formats, deferred issuance, notifications, status or revocation, persistence, and multiple replicas. This is a profile implementation claim, not full issuer certification or conformance. External Inji interoperability evidence is candidate-only until a frozen release artifact records the pinned client revisions and reproducible result.

name: SD-JWT VC
version_or_profile: Profiled subset using the `application/dc+sd-jwt` media type and `dc+sd-jwt` JWT `typ` (no specific IETF draft revision pinned by the implementation)
surfaces: shared SD-JWT VC issuance and holder-proof helpers
Evidence Gateway SD-JWT VC response format
holder-bound subject binding and key-binding JWT presentation verification

evidence_docs.label: Evidence Gateway strict verification policy schema
Evidence Gateway portable SD-JWT VC verifier
Registry Notary SD-JWT VC conformance profile

notes: Registry Platform owns reusable SD-JWT VC issuance and holder-proof helpers. Evidence Gateway serializes its stateless assertion as an SD-JWT VC under its own frozen profile, and that profile is the source of truth for the claim set it emits. Two subject binding modes exist. Under the default audience-scoped mode the credential is meaningful only to the relying party the assertion names, and a caller-supplied holder key is echoed into `cnf` unverified. Under the declared holder-bound mode the binding derives from the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder key, `cnf` is required, and possession is proven at presentation by a key-binding JWT under RFC 9901 section 4.3 rather than by the audience at issuance. Verifying a key-binding JWT proves possession at signing time over the presented bytes; comparing its nonce is not consuming it, so nothing here is replay prevention. The holder-bound profile document and its verification policy schema are not yet on a citable commit, so no evidence link pins them. Registry Notary owned the claim-to-credential workflow and the service routes that used them, and is retired; its pinned conformance profile and format constants are kept as the record of that workflow. The Registry Platform helpers stay constrained: `application/dc+sd-jwt` credentials, issuer signing with EdDSA over Ed25519 or ES256 over P-256, and EdDSA `did:jwk` holder binding. The retired product also rejected pre-rename format aliases such as `application/vc+sd-jwt` in operator configuration. Full SD-JWT VC conformance is not claimed, and the Evidence Gateway runtime implements OID4VCI in no part; wallet-facing OID4VCI delivery of an Evidence credential belongs to the separate `registry-evidence-oid4vci` front end, which this record does not cover.
